findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Observed at least two leaks dripping from the faucets of the triple sink. Discussed and shown to PIC. PIC mentioned that she would contact the facility’s internal maintenance team to repair the leaks. Ensure that faucets are maintained in leak free condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The soda nozzles at the drive thru’s soda machine were observed to have soil build-up. Discussed with PIC and nozzles were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that soda nozzles are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil buildup. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Nozzles and diffusers at drive thru soda machine were soiled with varying amounts of mold buildup, some of which was getting rather thick. Nozzles and diffusers were cleaned and sanitized during inspection. Ensure cleaning occurs on a more frequent basis/as needed to eliminate buildup.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee removed a single use glove to open a door and then put the glove back on to finish preparing an order. Proper use of gloves was discussed. Employee washed hands and put on a new pair of gloves prior to continuing with next task. Ensure proper glove use and be mindful that glove changes are needed after personal habits occur, such as adjustment of clothing, hats, glasses, etc.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floors in the following areas were observed to be soiled:
1) under lobby soda counter (general buildup/splash);
2) under make line (general buildup);
3) under dry storage shelves (onions and general debris buildup);  and
4) under ice machine and to the left around the corner by reach-in cooler (ponding water and general debris).
Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas and throughout the facility as needed.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the lid to the ice cream machine to not be on the machine. The lid was set on top of the slushy machine. Ensure the lid is placed on the ice cream machine to protect the mix from contamination. The lid was placed on the machine during the inspection. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the lemonade and root beer soda nozzles to be soiled. Ensure soda nozzles and other equipment are cleaned frequently so they are clean to sight and touch. The soda nozzles were cleaned during the inspection to correct the violation. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop to be stored inside the mop bucket with old mop water in it during the inspection. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to air dry and old mop water is discarded after use. Mop was moved during the inspection. 
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: Observed multiple mops throughout the facility to be sitting inside the mop bucket with old mop water in them. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to drip dry and mop water is discarded after it is used. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by a box of tomatoes . Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Observed a cooler that held a temperature of approximately 55 degrees. Pies were observed at a temperature of 55 degrees. The containers for the pies stated that they should be refrigerated. Pies were placed in the fridge at 7:00 am and should be discarded at 11:00 am. No TCS foods should be stored in this fridge until it is fixed.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) Observed employee coats hung above buns in a dry storage area. Employee coats and other personal items should be hung away from food and food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
findings.comment:
Trigger attached to hose beneath Y connector on mop sink.  No dedicated line to chemical dispenser.

750-1060 There shall be no cross-connection between the safe-water supply and any unsafe or questionable water supply, or any source of pollution through which the safe water supply might become contaminated. Abate in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the mop rack to be bare, unsealed wood. Maintenance is on site today with plans to replace this wood rack with something that is smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the tops and dividers in the hot holding units on the make line with grease accumulation, 2) the top inside of the microwave on the make line to be soiled with food debris accumulation. Wash, rinse and sanitize these food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the shelves above the three compartment sink with dripping grease, 2) the lids to the fryers in storage for the day with grease and food debris accumulation, 3) the table behind the coffee maker with coffee grounds, 4) the area underneath where the fryer baskets are taken out of the fryers (above the chest freezer with the onion rings in it) with food debris accumulation. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
1) Observed coffee filters stored unprotected on a shelf in the dry storage area. 2) Observed straws stored underneath the drain lines at the soda fountain in the dining area. 3) Observed a box of lids stored underneath the black refrigerated lines that are dripping under the soda fountain in the dining area. Lids were discarded. Store single service items protected and in areas away from plumbing.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
1) Observed the knee paddle at the hand sink in the back to stick at times and the water to trickle when off. 2) Observed the faucet on the right at the three compartment sink to be leaking. 3) Observed the black wrapped pipes underneath the soda fountain in the dining area to be leaking. This soda fountain also has a drip from when the ice bin on top is over filled, and there is a pan on the floor to collect the drips. Maintenance is on site and is going to address these issues. Repair these leaks.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed an employee purse to be stored in a box with paper towels in the back storage room. Store personal belongings in areas away from food and single service items.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No proof of IL FSSMC at this time. Manager Greg Foster has proof of NRFSP exam completion, and submitted his information in writing to the State who in turn returned it and instructed him to submit it online. Submit information online and provide inspector with IL certificate once received. 
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed mocha and strawberry banana puree in the reach in cooler at the front counter to be dated marked with a Use Thru date of 11/7. These items were discarded during the inspection to correct the violation as they were passed the 7 days allowed.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment:
Observed a container of ham that had a Time as a Control expiration time of 10:00 AM around 10:30 AM, however an employee states that the ham had just been restocked. Apparently the ham had been re-stocked in the same container that had been out for the previous 4 hour period and had not been washed, rinsed and sanitized in between use as the old time sticker was still intact. Employee discarded ham in this container and the issue was discussed.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
REPEAT> 1) Observed the handle to the walk in cooler to be broken in half. Repair of replace handle making sure that it is free from unnecessary crevices. 2) Observed the lid of the chicken reach in freezer to be broken/cracked. Replace lid. NEW> Observed the rack used for hanging mops near the mop sink to be raw wood. Paint or seal wood. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the soda fountain nozzles and area around the nozzles with what appears to be mold, 2) the coffee maker spout at the drive thru is soiled black, 3) the tops of the hot holding unit where the trays are inserted with food debris and grease accumulation.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the shelves above the three compartment sink with dripping grease, 2) the inside of the convection oven with grease and char, 3) the handle to the microwave with food debris accumulation, 4) the sides of equipment such as the bun toasters with grease and dust accumulation, 5) the fan in the reach in cooler underneath the ice cream machine with dust accumulation. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service containers stored food contact surface up on top of the hot holding units and on the dry storage shelves in the back. Store single service items inverted with the food contact surface protected from potential contamination.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
1) Drive thru hand sink did not have a supply of paper towels available. Provide paper towels. 2) Observed the women's restroom to not have a covered waste can. Provide a covered waste can in the restroom.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
REPEAT> 1) Observed the caulk at the urinal to be cracked and missing. Re-caulk urinal to the wall. NEW> 2) Observed the caulk at the mop sink to be separating. Re-caulk mop sink to the wall. 3) Observed the wall behind the prep sink to be soiled with food splash. Clean the wall. 4) Observed a hold in the wall in the women's restroom to the right of the hand sink. Fix hole.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed personal belongings such as jackets and coats stored hanging on dry storage racks and sitting on empty bun racks in the back room. Provide sufficient space for employee belongings so that these items are not being stored in contact with food or single service items for the facility.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed mops stored with the mop head down in the mop bucket. Store mops hanging or inverted to dry.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No proof of IL FSSMC on site at the time of the inspection. Manager Marquis knows that he has his ServSafe certificate but does not know about the IL certificate. Provide inspector with proof of IL certificate.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
1) Observed burgers unprotected in the bottom of the reach in burger freezer. 2) Observed several bags of items such as burgers, chicken, lettuce, buns that are open and not protected. Fold bags over to protect from potential contamination.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed the handle to the walk in cooler to be broken in half. Repair or replace handle making sure that it is smooth and easily cleanable. 2) Observed the lid of the chicken reach in freezer to be broken. Repair lid.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) CORRECTED> Observed the inside of the egg cooker (the grid part) to be soiled with grease accumulation. Cooker was cleaned during inspection. 2) The inside of the microwave including the top inside surface with food splatter. Clean the microwave.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the shelves above the three compartment sink are sticky 2) the tongs and the ledge on the prep line with grease accumulation, 3) the hot holding units and in between the units and the plugs on the units with food debris and grease 4) the tape dispenser near the veggie sink with ketchup accumulation, 5) the inside of the vegetable prep sink with food debris 6) the inside and outside handles of the fryer cabinets with grease accumulation 7) the inside of the convection oven with food debris and char 8) the side of the bread toaster with grease 9) the fry reach in freezer heavily soiled with food debris inside and outside 10) the ledges of the bread racks with food debris 11) the outside edges of the burger reach in freezer with food debris 12) the inside of the burger reach in freezer with ice accumulation 13) the mop sink with food debris 13) the insides of the fry container dispensers with build up. Clean all non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service articles stored on the dry storage shelves unprotected with the food contact surface up. Store single service articles inverted.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink next to the three compartment sink to be leaking. Repair hand sink.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floors to be soiled in the following areas: 1) under the bag in box soda shelves, 2) under the front counter areas, 3) in front of the fryers. Clean the floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the walls to be soiled in the following areas: 1) above the three compartment sink, 2) behind the bag in box soda. 3) Observed the caulk at the urinal to be cracked and missing. Clean the walls and reseal urinal to the wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a pickle bucket full of salt that was not labeled with its contents. Bucket was labeled during inspection.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
1) Observed wet mops stored in the mop bucket. Hand or invert mops to dry in between use. 2) Observed extra equipment such as a prep table in the dry storage area that is not in use. Remove equipment from premises if not being used.
750-1350c Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
